title: Torres del Paine National Park
description: Renowned for its stunning granite peaks, glaciers, and diverse wildlife, offering some of the best hiking trails in the world.
hikingExplained: Chile's Torres del Paine National Park showcases a breathtaking blend of glaciers, towering peaks, and serene lakes. The W Circuit hike traverses through an array of landscapes, from the iconic granite spires known as the Torres to vast valleys adorned with electric-blue icebergs. Each turn on this trek offers stunning vistas, crossing diverse terrain that includes dense forests, tranquil lakes like Nordenskjöld, and the challenging but rewarding climb to the base of the iconic towers themselves.

photo.alt: Torres del Paine National Park, Chile

details.permit: Park entry ticket bought online in advance; every campsite or refugio night must be booked before you arrive.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales, then take the bus to Laguna Amarga (about 2 hours from Puerto Natales).
tips: Book campsites months ahead for December–February.
Wind above 80 km/h is common — pack a windproof shell and trekking poles.

title: Machu Picchu
description: Ancient Incan city nestled in the Andes Mountains, surrounded by breathtaking scenery and hiking trails like the Inca Trail.
hikingExplained: Nestled high in the Andes Mountains of Peru, Machu Picchu stands as a testament to ancient Incan engineering and culture. The Inca Trail trek leading to this mystical city winds through mountain passes, cloud forests, and impressive ruins before finally revealing the awe-inspiring sight of the Lost City of the Incas. This challenging hike not only offers historical intrigue but also stunning natural beauty as it passes through diverse ecosystems and culminates with a sunrise view over the enigmatic ruins.

details.permit: Inca Trail permits are sold only through authorized agencies and spaces are limited; the trail closes every February for maintenance. Machu Picchu needs its own timed ticket.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Cusco; operators drive you to the trailhead at Km 82 near Ollantaytambo.
tips: Spend a few days around Cusco (about 3,350 m) to acclimatise before the high pass.
Bring your passport — it's checked at the trail and at Machu Picchu.

title: Banff National Park
description: A paradise for outdoor enthusiasts with pristine lakes, snow-capped peaks, and extensive hiking opportunities.
hikingExplained: Canada's Banff National Park is a picturesque haven for hikers, boasting turquoise lakes, rugged peaks, and abundant wildlife. Trails like the Plain of Six Glaciers lead through awe-inspiring landscapes of glaciers and alpine meadows, offering stunning vistas of the surrounding mountains and pristine natural beauty. The park's diverse terrain and well-maintained trails cater to hikers of various skill levels, providing ample opportunities to immerse in the grandeur of the Canadian Rockies.

details.permit: Parks Canada pass required for every visitor.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Calgary, then drive about 2 hours to Lake Louise; parking fills by early morning, so use the Parks Canada shuttle.
tips: The teahouse halfway up serves tea and cake — cash only.
Carry bear spray and know how to use it.

title: Yellowstone National Park
description: Home to geysers, hot springs, diverse wildlife, and numerous hiking trails through forests and canyons.
hikingExplained: America's iconic Yellowstone National Park is a geothermal wonderland, offering an array of hiking trails amidst bubbling geysers, colorful hot springs, and diverse ecosystems. The Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone presents dramatic vistas, with trails leading to majestic waterfalls and the fascinating geological features that define this unique landscape. Hiking here is an adventure through a land where nature's forces are on full display, creating an unforgettable experience for visitors.

details.permit: Park entrance pass; overnight trips need a backcountry permit.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Bozeman, Jackson or West Yellowstone; the Dunraven Pass trailhead is between Canyon and Tower.
tips: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer — be off the summit by early afternoon.
Bighorn sheep and grizzlies live on the slopes; carry bear spray.

title: Serengeti National Park
description: Famous for the annual wildebeest migration, offering vast plains and exceptional wildlife viewing on foot or via safaris.
hikingExplained: Tanzania's Serengeti National Park is a sprawling savanna renowned for the Great Migration and its diverse wildlife. Hiking through this iconic landscape offers encounters with lions, elephants, and wildebeests in their natural habitat. The vast plains, framed by golden grasses and acacia trees, create an immersive experience in the heart of Africa's wilderness.

details.permit: Walking is only allowed with an armed park ranger; park fees are paid per day.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Kilimanjaro or Arusha, then a light aircraft or a long drive to the park.
tips: Book walks through your lodge or operator — they arrange the ranger.
January–February is calving season in the south; June–October is the dry season.

title: Table Mountain National Park
description: Iconic mountain with diverse flora and fauna, featuring hiking trails and panoramic views of Cape Town and the coast.
hikingExplained: Overlooking Cape Town, South Africa, Table Mountain National Park features an array of hiking trails winding through fynbos-covered slopes. These trails offer panoramic views of the city, coastline, and unique rock formations, providing hikers with a mix of natural beauty and cultural significance.

details.gettingThere: Start from Tafelberg Road in Cape Town; ride the cable car down if it's running.
tips: Check the cable car status before you go — wind closes it and the 'tablecloth' cloud rolls in fast.
Start early in summer; there's almost no shade.

title: Sapa
description: Stunning terraced rice fields, ethnic villages, and challenging trekking routes in the Hoàng Liên Son Mountains.
hikingExplained: Nestled in the mountains of Vietnam, Sapa is famed for its terraced rice fields and ethnic minority villages. Hikes here unveil breathtaking landscapes and cultural encounters with local hill tribes. The trails meander through lush greenery and misty valleys, offering glimpses into traditional rural life and panoramic vistas of the surrounding mountains.

details.route: Sa Pa to Lao Chai and Ta Van
details.permit: Small village entry fee for the Muong Hoa valley; local guides are recommended.
details.gettingThere: Night train or bus from Hanoi to Lao Cai, then 1 hour by road to Sa Pa (about 5–6 hours by direct bus).
tips: Rice terraces are greenest in June–July and golden in September.
Trails turn to mud after rain — wear shoes with grip.

title: Annapurna Circuit
description: One of the world's classic treks, circling the Annapurna Massif, showcasing diverse landscapes and rich culture.
hikingExplained: Circumnavigating the Annapurna Massif in Nepal, this trek is renowned for its varied landscapes, from lush forests to arid high-altitude terrain, and diverse cultures encountered in the villages along the way. Hikers traverse deep gorges, cascading waterfalls, and mountain passes like Thorong La, soaking in the majestic Himalayan scenery and the warm hospitality of local communities.

details.permit: ACAP permit and TIMS card; since 2023 foreign trekkers must hike with a licensed guide.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Kathmandu, then bus to Besisahar (about 7 hours) to start.
tips: Build in rest days at Manang to acclimatise before Thorong La.
Cross the pass at dawn, before wind picks up.

title: Fiordland National Park
description: A land of fiords, waterfalls, and dramatic landscapes with multi-day hiking trails like the Milford Track.
hikingExplained: In New Zealand, Fiordland captivates with its deep fjords, cascading waterfalls, and ancient forests. Hiking trails like the Milford Track offer a glimpse into the region's pristine wilderness, with opportunities to witness breathtaking landscapes and encounters with unique wildlife amid the tranquility of this remote corner of the world.

details.permit: Great Walk season (late October–April): huts must be booked with DOC; walk one way only, north to south.
details.gettingThere: Te Anau is the base; a bus and boat take you to Glade Wharf at the head of Lake Te Anau.
tips: Bookings open months ahead and sell out within hours.
It's one of the wettest places on Earth — waterfalls are best on rainy days.

title: Kakadu National Park
description: Boasting diverse ecosystems, Aboriginal rock art, and walking trails showcasing unique wildlife and landscapes.
hikingExplained: Australia's largest national park, Kakadu, showcases diverse landscapes, from wetlands to sandstone escarpments. Hikes here reveal Aboriginal rock art, stunning waterfalls, and unique wildlife. Exploring this vast terrain provides insight into both the cultural heritage and natural beauty of the Northern Territory.

details.permit: Kakadu park pass required.
details.gettingThere: Drive about 3 hours from Darwin to Jabiru; Burrungkuy (Nourlangie) is 30 minutes south.
tips: Walk in the dry season and start at dawn — it gets very hot.
Respect closed rock-art sites; they are sacred to Bininj/Mungguy people.

title: Isle of Skye
description: Scenic isle with lochs, mountains, and forests, offering hiking, wildlife spotting, and stunning views.
hikingExplained: Scotland's Isle of Skye is a rugged paradise, featuring dramatic landscapes of jagged peaks, sheer cliffs, and picturesque lochs. Hiking trails like the Quiraing and the Old Man of Storr lead through enchanting scenery, offering panoramic views of the coastline and ancient rock formations that evoke a sense of otherworldly beauty.

details.permit: No permit needed.
details.gettingThere: Drive about 2.5 hours from Inverness, or take the train to Kyle of Lochalsh and drive over the bridge.
tips: Park early at the Quiraing car park; it fills by mid-morning in summer.
Midges bite from June to August — bring repellent.

title: Plitvice Lakes National Park
description: A series of cascading lakes and waterfalls amid lush forests, featuring picturesque hiking trails.
hikingExplained: Croatia's Plitvice Lakes National Park is a wonderland of interconnected lakes, waterfalls, and lush forests. Trails here wind through wooden walkways and bridges, allowing hikers to explore the park's natural splendor while witnessing the mesmerizing turquoise waters cascading between terraced pools.

details.permit: Entry ticket bought online with a timed entry in summer.
details.gettingThere: Drive or bus about 2 hours from Zagreb or Zadar; the park's boat and panoramic train link the routes.
tips: Arrive at opening time to have the boardwalks to yourself.
Swimming is not allowed anywhere in the park.

title: Los Glaciares National Park
description: Home to the famous Perito Moreno Glacier and stunning landscapes ideal for hiking and glacier exploration.
hikingExplained: Argentina's Los Glaciares National Park is home to the iconic Perito Moreno Glacier and a network of stunning trails that offer close encounters with the park's namesake glaciers. Hiking here presents awe-inspiring views of towering ice walls, glacial lakes, and the breathtaking beauty of Patagonia's rugged landscapes.

details.route: Laguna de los Tres from El Chaltén
details.permit: El Chaltén trails are free; the Perito Moreno glacier sector charges an entry fee.
details.gettingThere: Fly to El Calafate, then bus about 3 hours to El Chaltén.
tips: The last kilometre is very steep — poles help.
Watch for clear-weather windows; Fitz Roy can hide in cloud for days.

hikingExplained: Tasmania's Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park boasts ancient rainforests, alpine heaths, and glacial lakes. Hiking trails like the Overland Track traverse diverse terrain, from serene lakes to rugged mountain landscapes, providing hikers with a unique glimpse into Tasmania's natural beauty.

Side trip: Mount Ossa, Tasmania's highest peak (1,617 m).

title: Kilimanjaro National Park
description: Home to Africa's highest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro, offering various trekking routes with stunning vistas.
hikingExplained: Home to Africa's highest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro, this park in Tanzania offers several trekking routes leading to the summit. Hiking through different ecological zones, from lush rainforests to alpine deserts, allows trekkers to experience varying climates and breathtaking vistas before reaching the iconic snow-capped summit.

details.permit: You must climb with a licensed operator; park and hut/camp fees are included in their price.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Kilimanjaro International Airport and stay in Moshi.
tips: Choose 7 days or more — slower climbs reach the summit far more often.
Summit night is very cold; bring a warm down jacket and spare batteries.

title: Cinque Terre National Park
description: Picturesque coastal villages connected by hiking trails along the rugged Italian Riviera.
hikingExplained: Italy's Cinque Terre National Park is characterized by its colorful coastal villages, terraced vineyards, and scenic hiking trails along the Ligurian coastline. Trails connecting the five villages offer picturesque views of the Mediterranean Sea, charming villages, and terraced hillsides adorned with vineyards and olive groves.

details.permit: Cinque Terre Card required for the Sentiero Azzurro; some sections may close after storms.
details.gettingThere: Train to La Spezia, then the Cinque Terre Express that stops in every village.
tips: Walk Monterosso to Vernazza early, before the day-trip crowds.
Check trail status on the park site each morning.

tips: Check tide times — some crossings are only passable at low tide.

description: Sections of the iconic Great Wall surrounded by scenic landscapes and hiking trails.
hikingExplained: China's Great Wall is an ancient architectural marvel that spans thousands of miles across diverse landscapes. Hiking along sections like Mutianyu or Jiankou provides breathtaking views of this historic monument as it winds through mountains, forests, and picturesque valleys.

details.permit: Entrance ticket at the Jinshanling gate.
details.gettingThere: About 2.5 hours by car or tourist bus from Beijing.
tips: Jinshanling is partly restored — far fewer people than Badaling or Mutianyu.

title: Mont Saint-Michel
description: A medieval site amid picturesque landscapes.
hikingExplained: France's Mont Saint-Michel is an iconic island commune crowned by a medieval abbey. Hiking around this UNESCO World Heritage Site offers stunning views of the abbey, surrounding tidal flats, and the picturesque Normandy coastline.

details.permit: Cross the bay only with a certified guide — tides and quicksand are dangerous.
details.gettingThere: Train to Rennes or Pontorson, then the shuttle bus to the Mont.
tips: Walk barefoot or in old trainers; the sand is wet and muddy.
Guides set the time by the tide — book in advance.

title: Wulingyuan National Park
description: Majestic peaks, ancient pine trees, and stunning vistas in a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
hikingExplained: China's Wulingyuan National Park, home to the mesmerizing Zhangjiajie sandstone pillars, offers hiking trails through unique landscapes resembling something out of a fantasy. Trails like the Avatar Hallelujah Mountain Trail reveal towering stone pillars amid lush forests, providing a surreal experience for hikers.

details.permit: Multi-day park ticket covers the trails and shuttle buses.
details.gettingThere: Fly or take the high-speed train to Zhangjiajie, then about 1 hour to the Wulingyuan gate.
tips: Combine the stream walk with the Yuanjiajie pillars (the 'Avatar' viewpoints).
Mist often hangs in the valleys in the morning — beautiful but bring a light rain jacket.

title: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: It was built in a time when castles were no longer necessary as strongholds. Exceptional hiking experiences in the Alps.
hikingExplained: Germany's Neuschwanstein Castle, nestled in the Bavarian Alps, is surrounded by picturesque landscapes and enchanting trails. Hiking paths like the Marienbrücke trail provide panoramic views of the fairytale castle and the stunning Alpine scenery.

details.permit: Trail is free; castle tours need a timed ticket. The Pöllat Gorge closes in winter.
details.gettingThere: Train from Munich to Füssen (about 2 hours), then the bus to Hohenschwangau.
tips: Go early for the Marienbrücke view before the tour buses arrive.
Extend to the Tegelberg for views over the Alpine foreland.

title: Jiuzhaigou Valley
description: A nature reserve with crystal-clear lakes, waterfalls, and colorful landscapes in the Tibetan Plateau.
hikingExplained: China's Jiuzhaigou Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its turquoise lakes, multi-tiered waterfalls, and snow-capped peaks. Hiking through this scenic wonderland unveils breathtaking natural beauty amid the vibrant colors of the valley's lakes and forests.

details.permit: Entry ticket with a daily visitor cap; buy online in advance.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Jiuzhai Huanglong Airport, then about 1.5 hours by road.
tips: Ride the park bus up and walk the boardwalks down.
Autumn colours peak in mid-October.

title: Yosemite National Park
description: Home to iconic granite cliffs, waterfalls, and diverse ecosystems, providing exceptional hiking experiences.
hikingExplained: America's Yosemite National Park is a treasure trove of granite cliffs, waterfalls, and giant sequoias. Trails like the Mist Trail lead to iconic landmarks such as Yosemite Falls and Half Dome, offering hikers unparalleled views of the park's stunning landscapes.

details.route: Mist Trail to Vernal and Nevada Falls
details.permit: Park entrance pass; peak-season vehicle reservations may apply — check the park site.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Fresno (about 2.5 hours) or San Francisco (about 4 hours); YARTS buses run to Yosemite Valley.
tips: Waterfalls peak in May and June; the Mist Trail is slippery — rain jacket and good soles.
Come down the John Muir Trail for gentler grades and different views.

title: Ilha da Madeira
description: A beautiful island with a blend of mountains, forests, and waterfalls with hiking trails in a peaceful setting.
hikingExplained:
Portugal's Madeira Island boasts rugged coastlines, lush forests, and panoramic hiking trails. 
The levada walks, following irrigation channels, offer hikers access to the island's interior, showcasing its diverse flora and magnificent vistas of mountains and ocean.

details.route: PR1 Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo
details.permit: Non-residents pay a small trail fee online before walking official PR routes.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Funchal; Pico do Arieiro is about 40 minutes by car.
tips: Start before sunrise for a sea of clouds below you.
Bring a headlamp — the trail goes through tunnels.

title: Iguaçú Falls
description: A stunning complex of waterfalls on the border of Brazil and Argentina, surrounded by lush rainforest.
hikingExplained: Straddling the border of Brazil and Argentina, Iguaçú Falls is a natural wonder of cascading waterfalls set amidst lush rainforests. Hiking trails here allow visitors to experience the sheer power and beauty of the falls from various viewpoints.

details.route: Trilha das Cataratas and Argentine circuits
details.permit: Separate park tickets on the Brazilian and Argentine sides; bring your passport to cross.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Foz do Iguaçu (Brazil) or Puerto Iguazú (Argentina).
tips: Brazil gives the panorama; Argentina gets you close — do both.
You will get soaked at the Devil's Throat — protect your phone.

description: Spectacular mountain landscapes close to the city of Monterrey, with numerous hiking trails.

details.permit: Check access rules on the day; carry ID.
details.gettingThere: Fly to Monterrey; the trailhead is in Guadalupe, on the city's eastern edge.
tips: Start before dawn — summer afternoons are extremely hot.
Carry at least 3 litres of water; there is none on the trail.

details.gettingThere: Bus from Salvador to Lençóis (about 6 hours), the base for the park.
tips: Families in the valley host trekkers — bring cash for meals and beds.
Add the Cachoeira da Fumaça viewpoint on the way.

description: An archipelago known for its pristine beaches, crystal-clear waters, and exceptional marine biodiversity.

details.route: Trilha dos Golfinhos to Baía do Sancho

details.gettingThere: Flights from Recife or Natal; visitor numbers are limited.
tips: Spinner dolphins gather in the bay early in the morning.
Book the guided trails (Atalaia, Capim-Açu) as soon as you arrive.

details.route: Atins to Santo Amaro dune crossing
details.permit: Hike with a local guide — there are no marked trails across the dunes.
details.gettingThere: Fly to São Luís, then about 4 hours by road to Barreirinhas.
tips: The lagoons are fullest from June to September.
Walk at dawn and late afternoon; midday sand is scorching.

Leeches love the wet season — leech socks help.

title: Refugio Laguna Negra
description: A lakeside mountain hut above Bariloche, reached by a forest-and-scree climb in Nahuel Huapi National Park.
hikingExplained:
The trail to Refugio Italia (Manfredo Segre) on Laguna Negra starts near Colonia Suiza outside Bariloche. It climbs through lenga and coihue forest along the Arroyo Goye valley before opening onto granite slopes and the dark, still lake that gives the hut its name.

Most hikers go up and back in a long day; staying overnight at the refugio lets you catch sunrise on the lake and continue on the Nahuel Huapi traverse toward Refugio Frey.

title: Mount Hood National Forest
description: Old-growth forest, glacier views and the basalt curtain of Ramona Falls on the slopes of Oregon's highest peak.
hikingExplained:
Mount Hood National Forest wraps around Oregon's tallest volcano, an hour from Portland. The Ramona Falls loop is its classic day hike: a crossing of the glacial Sandy River, then a shaded climb through moss-draped firs to a 36-metre waterfall that fans over columns of basalt.

For bigger days, the Timberline Trail circles the whole mountain in about 66 km of meadows, glacier-fed creeks and ridge views.

details.gettingThere: Drive about 1 hour 15 minutes east of Portland via US-26 and Lolo Pass Road.
tips: The seasonal footbridge over the Sandy River is removed in winter — check before you go.
Arrive early on summer weekends; the lot is small.

title: Zion National Park
description: Sheer sandstone walls, slot canyons and the chain-assisted ridge of Angels Landing in southern Utah.
hikingExplained:
Zion Canyon was carved by the Virgin River through layers of red and cream Navajo sandstone. Angels Landing is its most famous hike: switchbacks up Walter's Wiggles, then a narrow fin of rock with chains bolted for support and drops of more than 400 metres on both sides.

The Narrows offers the opposite experience — wading upstream between canyon walls that close in to a few metres apart.

details.gettingThere: Fly to Las Vegas (about 2.5 hours) or St. George; the park shuttle runs through Zion Canyon most of the year.
tips: Without a permit you can still hike to Scout Lookout — great views, no chains.
Avoid the chains section in rain, ice or high wind.

title: Jumbo Pass
description: A short, steep climb to alpine meadows and a wall of glaciers in British Columbia's Purcell Mountains.
hikingExplained:
Jumbo Pass sits on the divide between the Jumbo and Glacier creek valleys in the Purcell Mountains, west of Invermere. The trail climbs quickly through subalpine forest to wildflower meadows, a small backcountry cabin and a panorama of hanging glaciers and granite peaks.

The drive in on rough forest service roads keeps it quiet — you'll often have the ridge to yourself.

title: Everest Base Camp
description: The classic two-week trek from Lukla through Sherpa villages and Sagarmatha National Park to the foot of the world's highest mountain, with Everest views from Kala Patthar.
hikingExplained:
The trek to Everest Base Camp starts and ends at Lukla, the airstrip known as the gateway to Everest. From there the trail follows the Dudh Koshi valley past Phakding and Monjo into Sagarmatha National Park, then climbs steeply to Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa market town where most trekkers pause for a few days to acclimatise. Beyond Namche the views open up to Thamserku, Kangtega and Ama Dablam, with Lhotse and Everest dominating the skyline ahead.

The route continues to the famous monastery at Tengboche, then up through Pangboche to Dingboche or Pheriche, Lobuche on the edge of the Khumbu Glacier, and finally Gorak Shep, the last settlement on the trail. From here you walk over the glacier to Base Camp and climb Kala Patthar, the viewpoint above Gorak Shep where generations of trekkers have stood face to face with Everest. Take it slowly: the altitude, not the distance, is the real challenge.

photo.alt: Yaks carrying loads along a rocky trail in Sagarmatha National Park, with snow-capped Ama Dablam under a blue sky
photo.author: Sangyam adventurer

details.route: Lukla to Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar
details.permit: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit: NPR 3,000 per foreigner per entry (NPR 1,500 SAARC nationals, NPR 100 Nepalis, under-10s free), sold at the Tourist Service Center, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or at the park entry point and checked at Jorsale. Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality also charges foreign visitors a local tourism fee. Nepal Tourism Board lists the Everest Base Camp Trek among routes requiring a licensed guide and an agency-issued TIMS card (rule effective 31 March 2023).
details.gettingThere: Fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (Tenzing-Hillary Airport), the usual start. With more time you can walk in from Jiri through the Solu hills, which adds roughly 10 days but helps acclimatisation.
tips: Spend a couple of nights in Namche Bazaar and take day walks to Syangboche, Khumjung or Khunde to acclimatise before going higher.
Build in a second acclimatisation day at Dingboche; the side trip to Chhukung is a good way to spend it.
The final stretch over the Khumbu Glacier to Base Camp can take up to five hours on slippery, shifting ground, so start early and watch your footing.

title: Glacier National Park
description: Montana's 'Crown of the Continent': jagged peaks, glacier-carved valleys and alpine meadows, best walked on the Highline Trail, which traces the Garden Wall north from Logan Pass on the Continental Divide.
hikingExplained:
Glacier National Park in northwest Montana protects a wild stretch of the northern Rockies, with more than 700 miles of trail threading through glacier-carved valleys, alpine meadows and turquoise lakes. Our pick is the Highline Trail, which starts across Going-to-the-Sun Road from the Continental Divide sign at Logan Pass and runs along the Garden Wall, high above the valley, with big views nearly the whole way.

Most hikers go one way from Logan Pass to The Loop, a full day of about 19 km with more descent than climb, passing Granite Park Chalet near the end. Much of the trail is exposed, so it suits sure-footed hikers in settled weather; a shorter option is to walk out from Logan Pass for a while and turn back. Plan your transport ahead, carry bear spray and plenty of water, and watch for mountain goats and bighorn sheep.

photo.alt: A hiker in a red jacket looks out from the Highline Trail over a deep glacial valley and clouded peaks in Glacier National Park
photo.author: NPS / Jacob W. Frank

details.route: Highline Trail: Logan Pass to The Loop
details.permit: Park entrance pass required. No vehicle reservations in 2026, but from July 1 to September 7, 2026 Logan Pass parking is limited to 3 hours, so Highline hikers need a ticketed Logan Pass Shuttle seat booked on Recreation.gov.
details.gettingThere: Logan Pass is on Going-to-the-Sun Road, usually fully open from early July to mid-October. In summer 2026, ticketed express shuttles run to Logan Pass from Apgar, Lake McDonald Lodge, St. Mary and Rising Sun, and stop at The Loop to take hikers back.
tips: Book Logan Pass Shuttle tickets early: some are released 60 days ahead, the rest at 7 p.m. MDT the day before. Don't count on the last shuttle from The Loop.
The Loop has restrooms but no drinking water, so carry all the water you need from Logan Pass.
Much of the trail is exposed to drop-offs and weather; start early, check the forecast and carry bear spray.

title: Grand Canyon National Park
description: Arizona's mile-deep canyon of layered red rock, where steep, well-built trails drop from the South Rim into a vast inner world of buttes, ridges and the Colorado River.
hikingExplained:
The South Kaibab Trail is the Grand Canyon's classic ridge-line descent. It leaves the South Rim near Yaki Point and follows open ridges instead of side canyons, so the views start almost immediately: Ooh-Aah Point after 0.9 miles, Cedar Ridge at 1.5 miles, and Skeleton Point at 3 miles, where the Colorado River first comes into sight. The National Park Service names Skeleton Point as the farthest sensible turnaround for a day hike; the full 6.3-mile descent to the river is a backpacking trip that needs an overnight permit.

Everything here works in reverse: the easy part comes first and the climb out comes last, at altitude and often in strong sun. The trail has no water and very little shade, so carry all you need, turn around early, and plan on the way up taking about twice as long as the way down. In summer, rangers advise going no farther than Cedar Ridge; spring and autumn are the comfortable seasons, and the upper switchbacks can be icy in winter.

photo.alt: View into the Grand Canyon from the South Kaibab Trail: a scrub-covered ridge leads to O'Neill Butte with layered red cliffs and the North Rim beyond under a blue sky.
photo.author: P. Hughes

details.route: South Kaibab Trail to Skeleton Point
details.permit: No permit needed for day hikes. A park entrance pass is required ($35 per private vehicle, valid 7 days; non-US residents aged 16+ pay an extra $100 per person). Camping below the rim needs a backcountry permit.
details.gettingThere: Drive to the South Rim of Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona and park at the Backcountry Information Center. Private vehicles are not allowed at the trailhead: take the free Kaibab Rim (Orange) shuttle or the early-morning Hiker's Express to the South Kaibab Trailhead near Yaki Point.
tips: Allow about twice as long for the climb out as for the descent.
There is no water on the trail and very little shade: fill up at the trailhead and carry water and salty snacks for every person in your group.
Start early and turn around in good time. In summer, rangers advise not going past Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles down), and never try to hike rim to river and back in one day.
Mules use this trail: step off on the uphill side, stay quiet and still, and follow the wrangler's directions until they have passed.

title: Tour du Mont Blanc
description: A legendary 170 km loop around the Mont Blanc massif through France, Italy and Switzerland — high passes, glaciers, alpine pastures and mountain refuges, usually walked in 7 to 12 days.
hikingExplained:
The Tour du Mont Blanc circles the highest mountain in Western Europe, crossing three countries in one great loop: France, Italy and Switzerland. The classic route starts in Les Houches and runs anticlockwise over Col de Voza to Les Contamines, up over the Col du Bonhomme and the Col de la Seigne into Italy's Val Veny and Courmayeur, along the Val Ferret balcony beneath the Grandes Jorasses, over the Grand Col Ferret into Switzerland, through La Fouly, Champex-Lac and Trient, and back into France past Col de Balme and the Aiguilles Rouges.

This is not a technical climb, but it is a serious trek: roughly 10,000 m of ascent, a pass to climb and descend almost every day, and days of 5 to 8 hours with a pack. In return you sleep in mountain refuges and village guesthouses, eat well, and wake up to glaciers and granite spires each morning. Buses and lifts let you shorten stages, and many variants let you make it easier or wilder. Walk it in 9 to 10 days if you want time to enjoy the views.

photo.alt: A footpath crosses green alpine meadows toward the glaciated Grandes Jorasses in Val Ferret, Italy, under a clear blue sky
photo.author: Giorgio Galeotti

details.route: Classic TMB loop from Les Houches (anticlockwise)
details.gettingThere: Les Houches and Chamonix are on the Martigny–Le Fayet railway, and buses link the stages in the Chamonix valley. Courmayeur is reached from Chamonix by bus through the Mont Blanc tunnel, and the Swiss stages are served by Swiss buses and trains.
tips: Book refuges early on the official site: popular huts fill months ahead, and bookings for summer 2027 open on 15 October 2026.
Go between mid-June and mid-September. In June and early season, expect snow on the passes (most are above 2,500 m), incomplete waymarking and fewer shuttles, so carry a map or GPS.
Bivouacking is regulated differently in each country and commune, and banned in places such as Chamonix and nature reserves; check the local rules before you take a tent.

title: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
description: Three giant limestone towers in the UNESCO-listed Dolomites, ringed by a classic high-alpine loop that reveals their famous 500-metre north faces.
hikingExplained:
The Tre Cime di Lavaredo are the icon of the Dolomites: three sheer towers of pale dolomite rock rising from high plateaus on the border between South Tyrol and the Veneto, inside the Tre Cime Nature Park and the Dolomites UNESCO World Heritage Site. The classic way to meet them is the loop from Rifugio Auronzo, which circles the whole massif without any climbing and stays above 2,000 metres the entire time.

We love how the walk saves its best for the middle: an easy track past Rifugio Lavaredo leads up to Forcella Lavaredo, where the north faces suddenly appear in full. From there you can continue to Rifugio Locatelli for the postcard view, then drop across the meadows and small lakes of the Langalm and return along the western side to the car park. Start early — this is one of the busiest trails in the Alps in summer.

photo.alt: The north faces of the Tre Cime di Lavaredo in late-afternoon light above green alpine meadows, Dolomites, Italy
photo.author: Alessandro Drago

details.route: Tre Cime loop from Rifugio Auronzo (trail 101 via Rifugio Lavaredo and Forcella Lavaredo, returning via trail 105 and the Langalm)
details.permit: No hiking permit needed. Driving to the Rifugio Auronzo car park uses a seasonal toll road from Misurina that requires an online reservation in advance (pass.auronzo.info); in 2026 a car costs €40 and the ticket is valid 12 hours from the booked entry time. The road reopened for the 2026 season on 23 May.
details.gettingThere: Drive to Lake Misurina (near Cortina d'Ampezzo and Dobbiaco/Toblach) and take the booked toll road up to Rifugio Auronzo, or ride the seasonal shuttle bus line 444 from Dobbiaco/Toblach to Rifugio Auronzo (timetables on sii.bz.it).
tips: Book your car-park slot online before you go — without a reservation you will be turned back at the toll gate; the bus avoids this entirely.
Arrive early: in peak summer the official advice is to be there before 7 am, when the trail and car park are still quiet.
You are walking at 2,200–2,450 m, where weather changes fast — bring a warm layer and rain jacket even on sunny days.
